The World Uyghur Congress, in its weekly brief, drew attention to developments concerning Uyghur human rights, cultural preservation and international pressure on China. The World Uyghur Congress, in its weekly brief, drew attention to developments concerning Uyghur human rights, cultural preservation and international pressure on China. According to the brief, the European Parliament adopted new recommendations on European Union-China political relations, calling for ties with Beijing to be based on respect for international law and human rights. According to the World Uyghur Congress, the recommendations recognised that three million Uyghurs had been subjected to forced labour and mass imprisonment. The Parliament called on China to end mass imprisonment policies and demanded the release of detained Uyghur scholar Ilham Tohti, Uyghur physician Gulshan Abbas, and the siblings of former World Uyghur Congress president Dolkun Isa.
